cases.name: invalid-json
cases.why: A payload that is not JSON degrades to a no-op. Hooks fail open: any internal failure still exits 0, because a broken guardrail must not wedge an editing session (SPEC.md section 7).

cases.name: not-an-object
cases.why: Valid JSON that is not an object is narrowed to an empty payload rather than indexed.

cases.name: unknown-keys-ignored
cases.why: Unknown keys are ignored, and an edit to a non-source file is a no-op — the narrowing half of the stdin protocol.

cases.name: stop-hook-active
cases.why: The infinite-loop guard: a Stop that follows a Stop this hook already blocked is a no-op, or a repo with one unfixable violation would block every stop forever.

cases.name: session-start
cases.why: The `hookSpecificOutput` envelope, which is what Claude Code reads `additionalContext` out of. Its content is summarized from the committed journal, so it is fixed.

cases.name: post-tool-use-block
cases.why: The blocking shape: `{"decision":"block","reason":...}` on exit 0, which is the only shape whose text reaches the model. The reason carries the rendered report, so the fixture's gates must fail — `apiKey = ""` in src/index.ts is the honest failure it blocks on. `live_durations` is set because the reason embeds the durations of gates that just ran; the SessionStart case leaves it off, because its numbers come out of the committed journal and are fixed.

notes: Every case exits 0. That is not laxity: Claude Code parses hook stdout at exit 0 and NOWHERE else, and treats other non-zero codes as advisory notices the model never sees, so a hook that returned 1 on failure would look installed and do nothing.

divergences.summary: SessionStart output: kragg-ts emits the `hookSpecificOutput` JSON envelope; Python prints plain-text context lines. Both are consumed by Claude Code, but only the envelope injects `additionalContext`. Candidate for convergence; not a bug on either side.

The hook checks what the equivalent `kragg check` invocation checks, resolved by `src/commands/scope.ts`: a Stop is the whole project (every `source_paths` entry), a post-edit is `check --file`, and a tool that edited no single file is `check --changed`. Python's `_stop` passes `source_paths[0]`. The stdout shapes below are unaffected, which is why this golden did not move.

Hook internal failures still fail OPEN (exit 0, nothing blocked, nothing added to stdout) but are recorded: a stderr line and an entry in `.kragg/hook-errors.jsonl`, reported by the next SessionStart. Python leaves no trace. The `session-start` case's context is unchanged here because this fixture's cases record no failures.

RECORDED DRIFT, not divergence: kragg-ts caps hook stdout at 9000 characters with an in-band marker because the harness spills longer output to a file the model never sees. Python does not truncate, so a very large failure report silently loses its blocking message. Do not remove the cap to match Python.
